title: The wedding night prayer (Tobit 8)
hook: Tobias and Sara pray together before anything else

segments.voice: Yesterday, Tobias set out with a dog and a guide who was really an angel. Your line was raphael walks with you. Who did you hold in mind on their journey? Day four hundred thirty-eight.

Remember Sara, the young woman in Media who prayed to die on the same day as Tobit? Here's why. She had been married seven times, and each husband died on the wedding night, before the marriage began, killed, the book says, by a demon named Asmodeus. Even her father's maid taunted her for it. Now Raphael brings Tobias to her father Raguel's house and tells him: she's your kinswoman, and you should marry her. Tobias has heard the stories. He's afraid. Who wouldn't be? Husband number eight.
screen: `SEVEN HUSBANDS, SEVEN WEDDING NIGHTS.` → `RAPHAEL SAYS: MARRY HER.` → `HUSBAND NUMBER EIGHT.`

segments.voice: Raguel agrees, the contract is written, there's a meal. Then the young couple are shown to their room. Tobias does what Raphael told him: he puts part of the fish from the Tigris on the coals, and the smoke drives the demon away, and Raphael binds it far off in the desert of Egypt. And then, before anything else, Tobias turns to his bride and says, in effect: Sara, get up. Let's pray, the two of us, that the Lord will have mercy on us. And they pray together. The prayer remembers where marriage began: God made Adam, and gave him Eve as a helper, and said it isn't good for the man to be alone. Tobias says he's taking Sara not out of lust but in truth, with a sincere heart. And they ask God for mercy, and to grow old together. In the Latin text the Douay follows, they go further and spend three nights in prayer before they sleep together. The Greek text, which most modern Catholic Bibles follow, keeps the prayer short. Either way, the first thing these two did as a married couple was pray. Meanwhile, down the hall, poor Raguel has been up in the night, quietly digging a grave, just in case. In the morning he sends a maid to peek in, and she finds them both asleep and well. So he has the grave filled in before anyone sees it, blesses God, and throws a wedding feast. This prayer of Tobias and Sara is one of the readings couples can choose for a Catholic wedding.
screen: `THE SMOKE, AND THE DEMON BOUND.` · `SARA, GET UP. LET'S PRAY.` · `MERCY, AND TO GROW OLD TOGETHER.` · `A GRAVE DUG, THEN FILLED IN.` · then, large: `BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE, THEY PRAYED.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: pray with someone you love, or hold them close in silence. Settle, and breathe. If someone you love is near you right now and willing, you could sit together and pray something you both know, an Our Father, or simply a moment of silence side by side. If you're alone, think of the person you'd most want beside you. A spouse, a parent, a child, a friend. Picture sitting down together before the day's business begins, the way Tobias and Sara did. If you pray, you can ask God's mercy on the two of you. The bell holds the time.
The wedding night prayer. Tobias and Sara, before anything else on their first night, pray together for mercy and to grow old together. Today's word.
Your line: pray together first. Today, before a meal or a big conversation with someone you love, stop for one shared moment first. Day four hundred thirty-eight.

howItsDone: The prayer of Tobias and Sara (Tobit 8) is among the Old Testament readings couples may choose for a Catholic wedding, and many Catholic couples make a habit of praying together.

fork.setup: you're Tobias. you've just married a woman whose seven husbands all died on the wedding night. you're alone with her now. what do you do first?
options: turn to her and say: let's pray together.
fork.reveal: before anything else, Tobias and Sara pray: they remember Adam and Eve, ask for mercy, and ask to grow old together.

trapdoor: what you thought: an odd story about a demon and a fish.
what it means: a frightened groom and a grieving bride begin their marriage with prayer, and wake up alive.
what a scholar hears: the Latin text adds three nights of prayer, the 'Tobias nights' of later custom; the prayer recalls Genesis 2:18, it is not good for man to be alone.

notes: All of Tobit 8 is paraphrased because the Vulgate/Douay and the Greek differ widely; no quotations.
Asmodeus kills the seven husbands (Tobit 3:8; 6:14). Confirm.
The three nights of prayer (Vulgate 6:18–22; 8:4) are not in the Greek. The 'Tobias nights' custom of medieval Europe is mentioned only in the trapdoor; confirm it's accurate or remove.
Tobit 8:4b–8 as an Old Testament option in the Order of Celebrating Matrimony: confirm.
'Not out of lust but in truth / sincerely' follows the Greek 8:7 and the Vulgate's 'not for fleshly lust' in paraphrase.
The practice suggests the Our Father (an existing prayer) or silence; no new prayer is written.
